entries.what_happened: None of the four manuscripts claims or proves that strong mixing implies strong 3-mixing. The link is a dependency on a companion. 'Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations' (MEA) and 'Pointwise convergence of fourfold ergodic averages for mixing transformations' (fourfold) both take as an input Theorem 1.1 of the companion 'Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation' (MixingCompanion, dated September 23, 2026; not in this family, not read). As the family restates it (MEA, build/sections/inputs.tex; fourfold, build/sections/02-structure.tex, eq. all-orders-input): for an invertible mixing probability-preserving T, any fixed s≥2, bounded g_1,...,g_s and integer times t_1,...,t_s, the integral of the product of g_j(T^{t_j}x) tends to the product of the integrals as min over i≠j of |t_i−t_j| tends to infinity. MEA's introduction calls this 'the assertion of Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem'. MEA uses it for all orders in its arbitrary-length selected-law argument (build/sections/channels.tex, correlation decay); the fourfold paper does the same (build/sections/05-channels.tex). What each manuscript itself proves: (1) MEA: for every n≥2 and bounded f_1,...,f_n, the averages (1/N) times the sum over k=1..N of the product of f_j(T^{jk}x) converge a.e. to the product of the integrals, along all positive integers N, for invertible bimeasurable mixing T on an arbitrary probability space, with no mixing rate. (2) Fourfold: the same for the times n,2n,3n,4n and four bounded functions. (3) 'Triple ergodic averages with distinct integer slopes': for three bounded functions at any three pairwise distinct nonzero integer slopes, positive or negative, the averages converge a.e. to the product of the integrals, under mixing. (4) 'Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations': the times n,2n,3n, a.e. on an arbitrary probability space with measurable inverse. Manuscripts (3) and (4) identify their limits using only two-function mixing (build/sections/transfer.tex, 'Identifying the limit by mixing', in (3); the Cesàro lemma in build/paper/sections/ergodic.tex in (4), an induction on pairwise correlations). Neither cites MixingCompanion.
entries.delivers: Nothing that settles Rokhlin's question. The family makes no 3-mixing claim of its own. Its bearing is conditional: MEA and the fourfold paper rely on the companion's all-orders statement, and no other manuscript in the family does. The companion's restated form covers the k = 3 case only in the min-gap sense: μ(A0 ∩ T^{-t2}A1 ∩ T^{-t3}A2) → μ(A0)μ(A1)μ(A2) as min(|t2|, |t3|, |t2−t3|) → ∞. The list's wording is different. It asks for convergence as the shifts m1 and m2 tend to infinity, with no condition on m1 − m2. The restated form does not cover shift pairs with m1 − m2 bounded, so as written it is weaker than the list's wording. The restated form is the usual k-fold mixing definition and covers all s, so it goes beyond the three-set case the list asks about.
entries.remains: Nothing of the problem is settled by this family itself. If the companion's Theorem 1.1 holds in the restated form, the min-gap version of the k = 3 case follows from it. That is the companion's claim, not this family's, and I did not assess it. The list's literal form (m1, m2 → ∞ with no gap condition) is not addressed by the restated companion form. The family's own results are pointwise a.e. convergence statements, not 3-mixing statements.
entries.direction: no direct claim on the question; pointwise convergence of multiple averages, conditional on an affirmative companion result
entries.conditional_on: MEA and the fourfold paper: MixingCompanion Theorem 1.1 in the restated all-orders form above, used for the selected-law and correlation-decay steps; not proved in this family. MEA also takes FourfoldCompanion Prop. 2.2 and Lemma 2.3 (relative structure and relative norm convergence) and SlopesCompanion Prop. 3.5, Lemma 3.6 and Lemma 3.9 (triple oscillation and profile approximation), and cites Austin's sated extensions. The fourfold paper also takes its analytic local estimates from TripleCompanion (manuscript (4) here) and HilbertCompanion ('An L^3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform', outside this family). Manuscript (3) takes its local estimates from H (the trilinear Hilbert paper, outside this family) and V (manuscript (4) here). Manuscript (4) takes its local estimate from H.
entries.doubts: (a) The theorem statements carry no conditional hypothesis, but the proofs rest on companion results not reproduced here. MEA says 'These companion proofs are not reproduced here.' The fourfold paper says 'The local analytic theorems themselves are cited with their hypotheses and locations.' Manuscript (3) says 'the technical part is a proof by reference to those manuscripts, whereas the ergodic deduction is presented in full', and describes its new estimates as 'extensions of the proofs in H, V, not new proofs of their coefficient-independent projection and row estimates.' (b) Manuscript (4) uses H's uniform local bound at one exponent q in (2,3) and justifies that choice by the parameter order in H's proof. (c) MEA's introduction calls FourfoldCompanion Theorem 1.1 'the fourfold mixing theorem', but in the fourfold manuscript that theorem is a pointwise convergence statement for four functions. (d) The restated companion form and the list's 3-mixing wording differ (see delivers).
